title: Frontend experience discovery
goal: Define the initial Ev Karnesi information architecture, navigation model, and user flows before page-level design.
constraints: Kapsam süre uğruna daraltılmaz; sıra bağımlılık, risk ve acceptance kriterlerine göre belirlenir.
Veri yokluğu düşük risk; bölgesel tehlike ise gerçek bina dayanımı olarak yorumlanmaz.
Her önemli türetilmiş sonuç kaynak, tarih, coğrafi çözünürlük, yöntem sürümü ve güven seviyesi taşır.
Her doğrulanmış write item docs/COMMIT_CONVENTION.md uyarınca atomik commit edilir; writer push yapmaz, accepted checkpoint'i üst orchestrator push eder.

decisions.summary: Use a floating three-action bottom navigation
decisions.reason: The user specified home on the left, search in the center, and profile on the right, visually grouped at the bottom center.

extensions.boundary: Page-level content and visual direction remain subject to user discussion.

decisions.summary: Support direct property research and area exploration as separate entry modes
decisions.reason: The user needs both exact address/building investigation and area-level searches such as Avcılar.

decisions.summary: Show the user's recent research instead of popularity content on the home screen
decisions.reason: The user rejected most-searched places as hard to establish and asked for a strong first-use empty state instead.

extensions.boundary: Page visual direction remains open for user review.

decisions.summary: Push the accepted frontend discovery checkpoint to origin/main
decisions.reason: The user explicitly requested commit and push for the completed documentation checkpoint.

extensions.boundary: Push to origin/main explicitly requested by user.

decisions.summary: Push the accepted additional frontend page briefs to origin/main
decisions.reason: The user asked to commit and push the completed page briefs before issue creation begins.

extensions.boundary: Push to origin/main explicitly requested by user.

decisions.summary: Use runs proportionally and batch low-risk design documentation
decisions.reason: The user asked that agents avoid creating run work items and results for every small page note, while retaining runs for cross-team coordination, major decisions, contracts, risk, and checkpoints.

items.title: Document initial frontend information architecture
items.objective: Record the agreed initial navigation model, core screen inventory, and high-level user flows before page-level design begins.
items.responsibility: Capture only the agreed product direction and open decisions; do not select a frontend stack, define data contracts, or implement screens.
acceptanceCriteria: The document names the agreed core screens and distinguishes account, search, report, saved, history, settings, help, and future plan areas.
The document defines a bottom navigation concept and the main flows for onboarding, direct property research, and area exploration.
Open product and design decisions are explicitly marked for the upcoming page-by-page discussions.

reasons: Planning artifact only; it does not make risk, score, or data-source claims.
approvalBoundaries: Page-level content and visual direction remain subject to user discussion.

items.title: Specify the home research hub
items.objective: Give frontend designers and developers an implementation-ready content, state, and interaction brief for the Ev Karnesi home screen.
items.responsibility: Define experience requirements only; do not choose a technology, invent ranking data, or implement UI code.

inputs.value: User direction for recent-search-first home content
inputs.description: Confirmed home-screen priority and empty-state direction

acceptanceCriteria: The page brief defines the home screen's hierarchy, entry points, content modules, and persistent navigation.
The brief separately specifies populated, first-use empty, loading, and recoverable error states.
The brief defines destinations and interactions without promising unavailable ranking or listing data.
The brief gives visual, responsive, accessibility, and copy constraints useful to a frontend team.

reasons: Experience specification only; no external data, scoring, or public risk claim is defined.
approvalBoundaries: Page visual direction remains open for user review.

items.title: Incorporate confirmed home-screen design decisions
items.objective: Update the home-screen brief with the user's confirmed content hierarchy and first-use decisions.
items.responsibility: Revise only the home-page documentation; do not implement interface code or decide unresolved error-map behavior.

inputs.value: User decisions on greeting, location detail, empty state, and saved content

acceptanceCriteria: The brief uses a named greeting and keeps recent-search location labels general.
The first-use state encourages research with a large illustration and primary property-location search action without leaving the page visually empty.
The brief removes a separate saved-items home module and marks map use in a recoverable error state as an implementation/design option.

items.title: Accept initial frontend discovery documents
items.objective: Confirm that the initial information architecture and home-page specification are ready for frontend design handoff.
items.responsibility: Assess the documented scope and checks; do not approve implementation, data contracts, or unresolved page design choices.
acceptanceCriteria: The documents agree on a mobile-only, three-action navigation and the two research modes.
The home brief covers the user-confirmed recent-research and first-use states.
Unresolved visual and implementation decisions remain labeled as open or delegated rather than silently decided.

items.title: Deliver initial frontend discovery checkpoint
items.objective: Commit and fast-forward push the accepted frontend discovery documentation to origin/main.
items.responsibility: Validate the accepted documentation commits and remote state; do not force-push or include generated run artifacts by default.
outputs: Commit SHA and origin/main push evidence
acceptanceCriteria: Outgoing commits conform to docs/COMMIT_CONVENTION.md and contain only the accepted documentation artifacts.
origin/main is fetched and the push is fast-forward without overwriting remote changes.
The checkpoint result records the remote, branch, and pushed SHA.

approvalBoundaries: Push to origin/main explicitly requested by user.

items.title: Specify the property search and map selection screen
items.objective: Define the mobile property-first search experience from administrative area selection through map pinning and editable building confirmation.
items.responsibility: Describe user experience requirements only; do not define geocoding, building identity, or map-provider contracts.

inputs.description: Confirmed city/district/neighbourhood selection and editable building confirmation

acceptanceCriteria: The brief makes property/building search the default mode and defines the city-to-neighbourhood, map, pin, and editable confirmation flow.
The brief covers the map and selection states needed by designers without inventing backend data behavior.
The brief specifies mobile interaction, accessibility, and open decisions.

reasons: Frontend experience planning only; geospatial identity is not being implemented.

items.title: Brief the report shell and supporting screens
items.objective: Give frontend developers directional briefs for the report shell and remaining supporting screens while preserving their design discretion where detailed content is not yet decided.
items.responsibility: State known purpose, routes, and constraints without prescribing unagreed fields, scores, or layouts.

inputs.description: Product report categories and user flows
Confirmed report placeholders and developer-led supporting screens

acceptanceCriteria: The report brief names only the currently agreed example categories and marks detailed report content as pending.
Saved, history, comparison, profile, settings, onboarding, help, and plans screens have clear purpose and design freedom boundaries.
The brief preserves product safety language and does not invent scoring or listing behavior.

reasons: UI planning only; no risk methodology is defined.

items.title: Accept additional frontend page briefs
items.objective: Confirm the property search, report shell, and supporting page briefs are ready for frontend handoff.
items.responsibility: Accept only planning artifacts; no backend, data, or scoring contract is approved.
acceptanceCriteria: Property search is property-first and preserves editable user confirmation.
The report and supporting briefs distinguish settled direction from design freedom and pending details.
The briefs are mobile-only and avoid unsafe or unsupported product claims.

items.title: Deliver additional frontend page briefs checkpoint
items.objective: Commit and fast-forward push the accepted additional frontend page briefs to origin/main.
items.responsibility: Validate the accepted documentation commits and remote state; do not force-push or include generated run artifacts by default.
outputs: Commit SHA and origin/main push evidence
acceptanceCriteria: Outgoing commits follow the commit convention and contain only accepted documentation artifacts.
origin/main is fetched and push is fast-forward.
The result records remote, branch, and pushed SHA.

approvalBoundaries: Push to origin/main explicitly requested by user.
